title: Automated compliance delivery workflows with attestations and selective redaction
creator: Anika Shah
description: Build a flexible delivery workflow for compliance reports (PDF/CSV) that supports scheduled and ad-hoc exports, tenant-scoped residency routing, signed attestations, and configurable redaction rules. The feature should power both the Console UI and the exports API and integrate with existing delivery channels (S3 presigned, HTTPS webhook, secure FTP). Focus on: (1) deterministic packaging of evidence and metadata, (2) a tamper-evident attestation artifact, (3) selective redaction per tenant/legal requirements, and (4) delivery audit trail and retry semantics.
background: Customers operating in regulated industries need periodic evidence packages for audits and the ability to automate delivery to third-party auditors or internal systems. Existing 'export snapshot' functionality is basic (single-tenant CSV zip) and lacks attestations, per-tenant redaction rules, and routing policies. This initiative combines product UX, export orchestration, and security controls to make scheduled reporting production-grade.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Admins can create a scheduled export job in Console that targets a tenant or tenant group, selects formats (PDF, CSV), and applies a redaction profile
AC2: Each export package includes a signed attestation JSON that contains input parameters, time window, residency region, and SHA256 checksums of each file
AC3: Exports can be routed to multiple endpoints with retry/backoff semantics: S3 (presigned), HTTPS webhook with mTLS option, and secure FTP
AC4: Delivery events are recorded in an immutable audit trail visible in Console per job and export (status: queued, in_progress, delivered, failed)
AC5: Redaction rules support field-level redaction, regex-based redaction, and policy inheritance; redacted fields are replaced with consistent tokens and recorded in attestation
AC6: Admins can trigger immediate replays (re-run) of a historical window; replay produces a new attestation referencing the previous export IDs
AC7: Scheduled jobs can be region-scoped so exported data never leaves the chosen residency region for that tenant
AC8: API-first: all UI operations are mirrored by /v1/compliance/exports endpoints with OpenAPI contract documented
AC9: End-to-end tests (integration) cover successful delivery, transient failures with retries, and redaction verification
api_contract: /v1/compliance/exports - POST/GET/PUT; documented OpenAPI in Confluence and Portal
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal beta): API + CL CLI trigger + single-tenant scheduled exports to S3 presigned - 2 weeks
Phase 2 (Pilot customers): Add attestations, redaction profiles, webhook delivery, and Console UI - 4 weeks
Phase 3 (GA): Add residency-scoped scheduling, FTP, mTLS webhooks, robust retries, and monitoring - 2 weeks
Canary rollout: enable for 5 pilot orgs, monitor delivery failure rate, and authorization errors before opening org-wide
notes: Trade-off: embedding signed attestations increases package size but provides cryptographic proof; consider optional attestation compression for large archives
Trade-off: performing redaction at export time vs storing pre-redacted artifacts. We'll redact at export time to minimize storage of PII and to respect changing redaction policies
Design decision: use HSM-backed signing (KMS integration) for attestations; fallback to application-level signing for pilot mode
Compatibility: output PDFs will be generated using the existing report renderer but need an upgrade to support page-level table-of-contents for long evidence bundles
implementation_notes: Add new export scheduler service with tenant-aware region routing and SLA-aware queues
Extend audit-log schema to include export_job_id, delivery_attempts, endpoint_response_code, and attestation_signature
Introduce a redaction engine with pluggable processors (regex, schema-based, ML-based PII detection) and deterministic tokenization
Use DAG-based packaging so each artifact (PDF, CSV, manifest, attestation) has a defined producer and checksum
qa_plan: Unit tests for redaction processors and tokenization deterministic behavior
Integration tests for S3 presigned delivery and webhook mTLS handshake
Compliance e2e: generate a 30-day window package, verify checksums against attestation, and exercise replay
Load test: schedule 200 concurrent export jobs and measure job queue latency and delivery throughput
observability_requirements: Metrics: exports_created, exports_failed, deliveries_attempted, deliveries_succeeded, deliveries_failed_by_code
Tracing: propagate export_job_id in distributed traces and surface long-running packaging spans
Dashboards: per-tenant weekly export volume, failure rate, average delivery latency
